ServicesOperations.HeadTitle: Operations platforms for service businesses | Ukrainian IT Family
ServicesOperations.MetaDescription: Invoicing, partner payouts, reconciliation and scheduling in one system where the numbers agree. Built for owners with no technical team. Scope in 48 hours.
ServicesOperations.PageTitle: One system where the numbers agree with each other.
ServicesOperations.PageDescription: Money in the bank, invoiced and earned. Three numbers that should match and don’t. We build the operations platform that makes them match, for owners who run the business without a technical team.

ProblemItems.title: The process lives in 4 places
ProblemItems.text: The schedule in one tool, invoices in another, partner payouts in a spreadsheet, the rest in someone’s inbox.

ProblemItems.title: A complaint means a recalculation
ProblemItems.text: A discount for the client, a new share for the partner, a new margin for you. All by hand.

ProblemItems.title: Month end takes a week
ProblemItems.text: And at the end of it nobody can explain why the figures differ.

ProblemItems.title: One person holds it together
ProblemItems.text: The whole process sits in their head. If they leave, so does the process.

ServicesOperations.ProblemClosing: None of this is a software problem yet. It becomes one the day you open the next city.
ServicesOperations.BuildDescription: Not a website in front of it. Every operations platform we build starts from how money and work move through your business today. Then we put it in one place.

BuildItems.title: Schedule and pricing rules
BuildItems.text: The schedule becomes the source of truth. Invoices, partner obligations and revenue come out of it, so they can’t disagree.

BuildItems.title: Invoicing and reconciliation
BuildItems.text: Bank transactions matched to invoices, including the payments that match nothing.

BuildItems.title: Partner payouts
BuildItems.text: Approval, corrections and recalculations in the system, not in a spreadsheet next to it.

BuildItems.title: One platform, every role
BuildItems.text: Admins, operators, partners, clients and back office. Each sees their part, nobody works in a separate tool.

BuildItems.title: Reporting
BuildItems.text: By city, country and period. The figure in the report is the figure in the system.

BuildItems.title: Room to grow sideways
BuildItems.text: A new city or country reuses the same core. You add data, not a new back office.

ServicesOperations.CaseTitles: Andulka: new cities, no new back office
CaseParagraphs: A property service business that grows across cities and countries through partners. Before the platform, invoicing, partner payouts and complaints lived in spreadsheets and bank statements, reconciled by hand. Every mistake cost money directly: a wrong payout, an unaccounted complaint, a wrong discount.

We built one system on a strict hierarchy: country, city, building, entrance. The schedule drives the charges. From it the system derives the client invoice, the partner payout and the service revenue. Complaints adjust discounts, partner income and margin automatically. DAC7 exports come from the same data.

CaseFacts.title: 1 source
CaseFacts.description: the schedule drives invoice, payout and revenue

ServicesOperations.CasesTitles: The same problem in other industries
FitYesItems: You run a team of 11 to 50 people.
Money moves through partners, payouts or several roles.
The process outgrew spreadsheets, and hiring a developer hasn’t worked or isn’t realistic.
FitNoItems: A ready SaaS fits your process as it is. Use it. We’ll tell you so on the call.

FaqItems.question: We tried this before. Nobody used the system.
FaqItems.answer: That usually happens when a system is built around how it looks, not how people work. We design for daily use: dense screens, filters that follow your process, the fewest clicks on the work your team repeats every day.

FaqItems.question: Our process isn’t standard.
FaqItems.answer: That’s the reason to build. If it were standard, a template would do, and we’d tell you to use one.

FaqItems.question: What will it cost?
FaqItems.answer: That’s what the 48 hour estimate answers, phase by phase, before you commit to anything. Phase one has a fixed scope and a fixed price.

FaqItems.question: Do we need a technical person on our side?
FaqItems.answer: No. You need someone who knows the process. The technical decisions are our job.

FaqItems.question: Can we start small?
FaqItems.answer: Yes. Phase one is deliberately small: the part of the process that costs you most today.

ServicesRegulated.ProblemTitles: The rule is clear. Following it by hand isn’t

ProblemItems.title: Reporting eats weeks
ProblemItems.text: Once a year someone pulls data from every system you have and hopes it adds up.

ProblemItems.title: One change, everything changes
ProblemItems.text: A supplier changes an ingredient, and every label, sheet and document that uses it has to change too.

ProblemItems.title: The record is somewhere
ProblemItems.text: In a PDF, an email, a spreadsheet. Finding it when someone asks takes a day.

ProblemItems.title: The mistake shows up late
ProblemItems.text: Not when it’s made, but when an inspector, a client or a court finds it.

ServicesRegulated.DomainTitles: Where the rules already live in our code
ServicesRegulated.DomainDescription: We don’t learn your regulation from a blank page. These are the rules we have already built into working products.

DomainItems.title: DAC7 and per-country reporting
DomainItems.text: Exports generated from the same data that drives invoices and partner payouts. No separate reporting project.

DomainItems.title: Food labelling
DomainItems.text: Allergens and nutrition calculated from nested ingredients. Change one ingredient and every product and label that uses it updates. Recipe sheets and labels come out as PDF, ready for internal control and audits.

DomainItems.title: Legally significant documents
DomainItems.text: Qualified electronic signatures, a secure archive, routing, access rights, audit logs and EDI integrations, sold as modules on one base platform.

DomainItems.title: Probation and court supervision
DomainItems.text: Case files bound to a person and a case. Monitoring that shows who needs attention right now, before a missed record becomes a legal problem.

DomainItems.title: DVLA plate transfers
DomainItems.text: Availability checked with the DVLA before the buyer pays. The transfer handled end to end, with status tracking in the back office.

ServicesRegulated.PrincipleTitles: How we build for regulated work

PrincipleItems.title: The regulated output comes first
PrincipleItems.text: The label, the export, the signed document. We design the system around the thing an inspector will read.

PrincipleItems.title: Every change leaves a trace
PrincipleItems.text: History and audit logs are part of the data from day one, not a feature added later.

PrincipleItems.title: Built for reality
PrincipleItems.text: Corrections, disputes, unmatched transactions. The system handles what goes wrong, not only the ideal case.

PrincipleItems.title: Checks before money moves
PrincipleItems.text: BigReg confirms availability before payment. Yachtomator validates every sum before a proposal goes out.

ServicesRegulated.CaseTitles: OffenderWise: where a missed record has legal consequences
CaseParagraphs: Organisations that supervise people under court and probation programmes track hundreds of people. Each has several cases, payments, restrictions, monitoring events and documents, spread across Excel, PDFs and email. The result is missed violations and legal exposure.

We built an operating system rather than a CRM. The supervised person sits at the centre. Cases, payments, monitoring, documents and time sit around them. Agents, supervisors and admins work in one environment, and the main screen answers one question: who needs attention right now.

CaseFacts.title: 9 core entities
CaseFacts.description: person, case, agent, project, document, payment, balance, monitoring event, time entry

CaseFacts.title: Daily use
CaseFacts.description: built for long term operational work

The cost of a mistake is a fine, a lawsuit or a lost client, not an awkward email.

FaqItems.question: Who is responsible for compliance?
FaqItems.answer: You are, with your lawyer or accountant. We make sure the system does exactly what the rule says and shows you the proof.

ServicesRescue.TriggerTitles: This page is for you if

TriggerItems.title: A contractor left
TriggerItems.text: And nobody can explain how the system works or why it was built this way.

TriggerItems.title: You hold a rewrite quote
TriggerItems.text: It’s a big number, and you want a second opinion before you sign.

TriggerItems.title: Real users broke the demo
TriggerItems.text: It worked in the presentation. It doesn’t work under real load.

TriggerItems.title: The project stopped halfway
TriggerItems.text: You need to know whether it can restart, or whether you’re paying to finish the wrong thing.

ServicesRescue.ArgumentTitles: The one purchase that can end with “don’t”
ArgumentParagraphs: A rewrite commits you to spending more. So does a refactor. An audit is the only thing you can buy where the best outcome is keeping your money.
Most contractors recommend the rewrite, because it’s the biggest contract on the shelf. We’re fine telling you to do less.
ServicesRescue.ArgumentQuote: A client came to us with a six figure quote for a full rewrite. After the audit, the part they wanted to rewrite turned out to be fine. The money stayed with the client.
ServicesRescue.DeliverableTitles: A priced decision, not a 40 page report
ServicesRescue.DeliverableDescription: A score out of 100 doesn’t tell you where to spend. A ranked list with a cost next to each item does.

DeliverableItems.title: What’s sound
DeliverableItems.text: The parts of the system that work and are worth keeping.

DeliverableItems.title: What nobody can explain
DeliverableItems.text: Code without an owner or a reason, and what that risk is worth to you.

DeliverableItems.title: What to fix and what to leave
DeliverableItems.text: Ranked by risk, with a cost next to each item.

DeliverableItems.title: The honest call
DeliverableItems.text: Refactor, replace in parts, rebuild, or do nothing yet. With the reasons.

AuditSteps.title: The call
AuditSteps.text: What the system does, who built it, what worries you. 30 minutes.

AuditSteps.title: Access
AuditSteps.text: Read access to the code and hosting. Nothing changes while we look.

AuditSteps.title: The decision
AuditSteps.text: A ranked list of problems with a cost next to each. If we wouldn’t spend the money, we say so.

AuditSteps.title: If you go ahead
AuditSteps.text: The team that ran the audit does the work. Or you take the list to anyone you like. It’s yours.

ServicesRescue.ProofTitles: We restart projects, not only review them

ProofItems.title: Restaurant marketplace, under NDA
ProofItems.text: An ageing framework migrated to its current version, technical debt reduced, and a new module that fills venue profiles from Google Reviews automatically. The platform got a base it can grow on.

ProofItems.title: The rewrite that didn’t happen
ProofItems.text: A six figure quote for a full rewrite. The audit showed the part marked for rewriting was fine. The client kept the budget.

FaqItems.question: You’ll tell me to rewrite everything anyway.
FaqItems.answer: A rewrite would be the bigger contract for us. That’s exactly why the audit has to be able to end with “don’t”. If the code is fine, you’ll hear it.

FaqItems.question: I’m not technical. Will I understand the result?
FaqItems.answer: Yes. Every item comes with what it means for your business and what it costs. No scores, no jargon.

FaqItems.question: Do you need the previous contractor?
FaqItems.answer: No. Access to the code and hosting is enough. If someone who worked on it is available, 30 minutes with them saves time.

FaqItems.question: What if the answer is a rebuild?
FaqItems.answer: Then you spend with confidence instead of hope. The point was never to avoid the rebuild. It was to avoid buying it blind.

productDevelopmentProjects.name: Andulka
productDevelopmentProjects.description: A property service business scaling across cities and countries through partners. Invoicing, partner payouts, complaints, and DAC7 reporting in one system of record.
productDevelopmentProjects.subtitle: Multi-country operations. Zero added back office.
problem: Money in the bank does not equal invoiced, and invoiced does not equal earned. Three numbers, and nothing explains the difference between them.

A service business delivered through partners has recurring payments, complaints, partner shares, service margin, and corrections. Without a system, it lives in spreadsheets and bank statements, reconciled by hand. The cost of getting it wrong is direct: a wrong payout, an unaccounted complaint, an incorrect discount. On top of that sits DAC7 and per-country reporting.
solutionIntro: One platform built on a strict asset hierarchy: country, city, building, entrance, services. The schedule is the single source of truth for charges: from it, the system derives the client invoice, the partner payout, and the service revenue.
solutionList: Hierarchical asset management down to the individual entrance
Automated scheduling and pricing rules per entrance
Invoice generation and bank transaction reconciliation, including unmatched payments
Partner payout approval with corrections and recalculations
Complaints processing that automatically adjusts discounts, partner income, and margin
Reporting by city, country, and period, plus DAC7 exports
approach: Built for people who use it every day. Dense, tabular, information-first. Filtering follows the domain logic instead of a generic dashboard. The fewest possible clicks on repeated operations, because a mistake here costs money.

Admin commands, recalculations, and imports run as background jobs, making it an event-driven system rather than a standard CRUD application. The interface is a projection of the data layer, not the other way around.
outcomes: Manual reconciliation across banks, invoices, and payouts is no longer a monthly ordeal
Reporting and payout figures no longer disagree silently
New cities and countries are launched without expanding back-office headcount
DAC7 compliance is handled fully inside the product

productDevelopmentProjects.closingQuote: The system is designed to work with reality: unmatched transactions, corrections, disputes. Not with ideal cases.

productDevelopmentProjects.name: Automarket
productDevelopmentProjects.description: An end to end automotive platform combining a marketplace, international import, financing and post sale services in one consultation driven journey.
productDevelopmentProjects.subtitle: A car becomes a supervised project, not just a commodity.
problem: Buying a car from abroad is a process with dozens of steps, low trust and opaque risk around customs, vehicle history and delivery. Nobody owns the whole chain.

For the dealer, the problem is the mirror image: selling the service chain rather than the car, scaling consultations without adding headcount, and capturing leads that would otherwise vanish into scattered messenger threads.
solutionIntro: The digital front office of a dealership business. The full vehicle lifecycle on one platform: cars in stock and to order, import from the US, Europe, Korea and China, financing, trade in, towing, storage and servicing.
solutionList: Catalogue in list and grid modes, technical filtering, availability status
Vehicle cards with photos, specifications, VIN, in stock or in transit
Import to order flows per source region, described step by step
Trade in, credit, towing, car park and service centre on one shared page pattern
Lead capture at every entry point
approach: Every action leads to a consultation, never to an unassisted order. One page pattern across all services: hero, value, stages, call to action. The catalogue works as a trust-building instrument, not as standard e-commerce. Detailed copy takes over part of the consultation, which lowers the load on both the buyer and the manager.
outcomes: Filters and content pre qualify the buyer before the call
Revenue beyond the vehicle margin: import commission, financing, add on services
Consultation capacity grows without adding managers
New countries and services are added without a redesign

facts.description: catalogue, import, credit, trade in, towing, service

productDevelopmentProjects.closingQuote: A case study about product thinking and business architecture for a service chain, rather than just UI.

productDevelopmentProjects.name: Menorika
productDevelopmentProjects.description: A multi-module digital platform for an art auction house, combining an online gallery, auction archives, artist database, paid access to historical sales data, courses, and institutional content within a single ecosystem.
productDevelopmentProjects.subtitle: Not just an auction website, but a comprehensive art market platform where data itself is the product.
problem: The true value of an auction house typically remains offline: sales archives, artist intelligence, catalogs, lot lists, bidding histories, and valuation expertise. Collectors and researchers struggle to find data on creators or past sales, while art trading, educational events, publications, and auctions operate in silos without reinforcing one another. Historical auction data holds real market value, yet cannot be monetized without a proper digital product.
solutionIntro: We built a centralized database of artworks, authors, auctions, and transaction histories, serving as the foundation for user-facing modules. The same piece of content can act as an author page, a gallery item, a sales archive entry, a ranking, an auction lot, a news post, or a course. This approach empowers a single institution to manage commerce, archives, research, and education from one unified system.
solutionList: Auction module: schedules, lot catalogs, results, and a comprehensive archive
Author database: biographies, currently available gallery works, and sales histories
Gallery e-commerce: filtering by price, size, category, and genre; favorites; and authenticated checkout
Paid data access: available per author, per auction, or as full access valid for 31 days
Rankings and market analytics: average artwork prices, trending authors, and highest-grossing lots
Courses and ticketing, publishing, plus a media and PR archive
Lost Art Items: a catalog of missing artworks to support provenance and restitution processes
approach: We implemented a complex relational architecture linking artworks, authors, lots, auctions, transactions, publications, and courses. A clear division between public and gated content: biographies are open, while sales histories require paid access. The checkout flow handles non-standard products, including physical artworks, data access, courses, tickets, and books. We also digitized decades of archives, providing pagination, indexing, and an admin-friendly interface for managing large datasets.
outcomes: New revenue streams beyond physical artwork sales: data access, courses, tickets, and publications
Historical auction data successfully transformed into a profitable digital product
Increased trust through open archives, detailed artist profiles, and transparent market histories
A content and SEO funnel that drives leads to a high-ticket business

productDevelopmentProjects.name: Expertland
productDevelopmentProjects.description: A structured marketplace for expert services, built around trust, multi level specialisations and controlled deals rather than a freelance bidding board.
productDevelopmentProjects.subtitle: $35,000 that replaced personal referrals.
problem: Businesses find it hard to locate verified experts. There is no fast way to hire without a long recruiting cycle, and there is risk on both payment and quality.
Experts face the mirror image. Chaotic inbound requests, no trust without ratings, and no structure connecting profile, specialisation, projects and payment.
solutionIntro: An ecosystem for interaction between business and experts, not a freelance exchange. Role selection drives onboarding. Category and specialisation limits control quality. A full lifecycle runs from registration to a completed project inside the platform.
solutionList: Expert onboarding and verification with a three level specialisation system
Expert profiles: education, languages, services and rates, portfolio, reviews, status
Project publishing with budget, languages, duration, screening questions and cover letters
Two catalogues, experts and projects, filtered by specialisation level, budget, country and business category
Project lifecycle management for current and completed work
Messaging with project context inside the conversation
approach: Four participants share one system: expert, client, company, and the platform itself. Taxonomy spans categories, specialisations, and business fields. Status scenarios cover profile activation and restriction. On top sits a trust layer and marketplace mechanics.
outcomes: A shorter path from a business need to a hired expert
Ratings, reviews and moderation replace personal referrals
The taxonomy scales into new domains without restructuring the catalogue

operationsProjects.description: A B2B SaaS for yacht charter brokers that turns raw yacht data, seasonal rates and fees into a correctly priced client proposal in minutes.
operationsProjects.subtitle: A request in. A finished proposal out. 5 minutes.
problem: Brokers assemble proposals by hand from Yachtfolio, spreadsheets, PDFs and memory. Calculations go wrong. Letters look different depending on who wrote them. A reply takes hours or days.
In this industry the speed of response decides the deal, the presentation carries the trust, and an error in the numbers is a reputational risk.
solutionIntro: A configuration driven quote builder. The broker picks a template, enters client data, dates and location, adds yachts manually or by import, toggles blocks such as fees, seasons and discounts, and gets a ready email or WhatsApp message.
solutionList: The Automator, a dynamic quote builder at the centre of the product
Centrally managed email templates with placeholders, fonts and accent colours
Financial rules: APA, per yacht VAT, high and low season, day and week rates, deposits, delivery and repositioning fees, discounts
Yacht data with URL based Yachtfolio import, manual override and multi currency
Contract Check, which validates sums, instalments and totals before sending
approach: A form first interface built around filling speed, not decoration. Detail work moves into modals so the main flow stays short. Checkboxes configure the output instead of duplicating forms. Imported data stays editable, so the broker can correct rather than trust blindly.
outcomes: Response time to a client request drops from hours to minutes
Pricing errors and missed fees stop happening
One standard of communication across every broker in the agency
New brokers can be onboarded without losing quality

operationsProjects.closingQuote: A configurable system built for a team, rather than a hard coded flow built for one user.

operationsProjects.name: Automarket
operationsProjects.description: An end to end automotive platform combining a marketplace, international import, financing and post sale services in one consultation driven journey.
operationsProjects.subtitle: A car becomes a supervised project, not just a commodity.
problem: Buying a car from abroad is a process with dozens of steps, low trust and opaque risk around customs, vehicle history and delivery. Nobody owns the whole chain.

For the dealer, the problem is the mirror image: selling the service chain rather than the car, scaling consultations without adding headcount, and capturing leads that would otherwise vanish into scattered messenger threads.
solutionIntro: The digital front office of a dealership business. The full vehicle lifecycle on one platform: cars in stock and to order, import from the US, Europe, Korea and China, financing, trade in, towing, storage and servicing.
solutionList: Catalogue in list and grid modes, technical filtering, availability status
Vehicle cards with photos, specifications, VIN, in stock or in transit
Import to order flows per source region, described step by step
Trade in, credit, towing, car park and service centre on one shared page pattern
Lead capture at every entry point
approach: Every action leads to a consultation, never to an unassisted order. One page pattern across all services: hero, value, stages, call to action. The catalogue works as a trust-building instrument, not as standard e-commerce. Detailed copy takes over part of the consultation, which lowers the load on both the buyer and the manager.
outcomes: Filters and content pre qualify the buyer before the call
Revenue beyond the vehicle margin: import commission, financing, add on services
Consultation capacity grows without adding managers
New countries and services are added without a redesign

operationsProjects.name: Real Estate CRM
operationsProjects.description: A B2B CRM for long-cycle sales in construction and infrastructure, built around real-world assets instead of leads.
operationsProjects.subtitle: The object appears before the deal does.
problem: Sales in construction run for months, are non-linear, involve many organisations, and often start without an inbound lead at all. The object exists before the deal does, and key decision-makers are rarely in the room.
Contacts, events and tasks scatter. Nobody can answer where a given object stands. Traditional CRMs force the team to adapt its workflow to a tool designed for short linear funnels.
solutionIntro: An object centric CRM. The object is the centre of gravity, and opportunities, counterparties, tasks, calls, meetings, comments, statuses, budgets and geography orbit around it.
One object holds many opportunities, each with its own lifecycle. The object outlives any single deal. It can go dormant and reactivate. Managers change, the history does not.
solutionList: Object creation or import with type, map location, description and budget ranges
Stakeholder binding: general contractor, subcontractors, partners, contacts
Opportunities per work type with status, budget and responsible manager
An automatic event timeline showing the real life of an object over time
Filtering by budget and partner, search, and soft pipeline logic
outcomes: Pipeline visibility across regions and distributed sales teams
Less context lost during long cycles and manager handovers
Better collaboration between sales and project teams
Higher quality forecasting and repeat sales on existing objects

facts.title: AUTOMATIC TIMELINE
facts.description: the real life of an object over time

operationsProjects.closingQuote: A CRM adapted to the real B2B sales process, instead of a sales process adapted to a CRM.

operationsProjects.name: Expertland
operationsProjects.description: A structured marketplace for expert services, built around trust, multi level specialisations and controlled deals rather than a freelance bidding board.
operationsProjects.subtitle: $35,000 that replaced personal referrals.
problem: Businesses find it hard to locate verified experts. There is no fast way to hire without a long recruiting cycle, and there is risk on both payment and quality.
Experts face the mirror image. Chaotic inbound requests, no trust without ratings, and no structure connecting profile, specialisation, projects and payment.
solutionIntro: An ecosystem for interaction between business and experts, not a freelance exchange. Role selection drives onboarding. Category and specialisation limits control quality. A full lifecycle runs from registration to a completed project inside the platform.
solutionList: Expert onboarding and verification with a three level specialisation system
Expert profiles: education, languages, services and rates, portfolio, reviews, status
Project publishing with budget, languages, duration, screening questions and cover letters
Two catalogues, experts and projects, filtered by specialisation level, budget, country and business category
Project lifecycle management for current and completed work
Messaging with project context inside the conversation
approach: Four participants share one system: expert, client, company, and the platform itself. Taxonomy spans categories, specialisations, and business fields. Status scenarios cover profile activation and restriction. On top sits a trust layer and marketplace mechanics.
outcomes: A shorter path from a business need to a hired expert
Ratings, reviews and moderation replace personal referrals
The taxonomy scales into new domains without restructuring the catalogue
